label: Change Communication Planner
description: Creates multi-channel, stakeholder-segmented communication plan for organizational changes. Sequences messages across channels (all-hands, email, manager cascade, FAQ) with timing and tone guidance.

claudeKnowledge.description: Change management communication (Prosci/ADKAR), organizational change communications, stakeholder engagement, change readiness

guidedInputs.label: Change description
guidedInputs.placeholder:
Describe the organizational change: what is changing, why, when, and the intended outcome.
e.g. We are merging the compliance and risk functions into a single Second Line of Defence department. The change is driven by regulatory pressure and internal efficiency. Effective 1 May 2025. Approximately 40 people affected. Department head: Sofia Lindqvist (current CRO). No job losses.

guidedInputs.label: Change effective date
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. 1 May 2025 (when the change takes effect operationally)

guidedInputs.label: Stakeholder groups
guidedInputs.placeholder:
List the key groups who need to be communicated with and their relationship to the change.
e.g.
- Directly affected employees (40 people): highest concern — role changes, reporting lines, team dynamics
- Wider organization (all staff): awareness and team context
- Management team: must align on messaging and handle team questions
- Board / Supervisory Board: governance notification
- External: regulators (FI) — notification may be required

options.label: Low — routine change, minimal concern expected
Medium — moderate change, some concern expected
High — significant change, high concern expected
Critical — major change with job security or major role implications

guidedInputs.label: Known employee concerns or resistance
guidedInputs.placeholder:
Any known concerns, rumours circulating, or resistance points that the communication must address.
e.g. Rumour that the merger will lead to job cuts. Concern that the CRO role outranks the current CCO (Sofia vs. Marcus). Teams have historically not collaborated well.
